result.title: Towards a Theory of Learnability via Debate
result.summary: Debate has been recently proposed as a training protocol that is hoped to produce more aligned models even as model capabilities scale. The idea is that the human, instead of providing supervision in the form of labels, judges a debate between two models that compete to prove the correctness of opposite labels. It can be shown that functions of a much higher computational complexity can be correctly judged in this way, compared to the complexity of functions that can be directly evaluated using a computationally weak evaluator. This suggests that perhaps debate can be used to teach very complicated functions to models. However, previous work has largely ignored the fact that this is a training protocol, and simply analyzes the game being played between the two debaters for a known judge. We take the first steps towards understanding the learning problem implicit within the protocol, by formulating it as an online learning problem. We show that once we formulate the learning problem precisely, there are cases where the best way to learn given access to a judge is different from running an adversarial debate. This motivates us to define a cooperative version of the protocol, whose learnability we characterize using a combinatorial dimension. We also consider the possibility of the human judge being fallible and occasionally judging the debate incorrectly. We show that a small number of errors in judgement can lead to a large error in learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「辩论」训练协议形式化为在线学习问题，指出在某些情形下最优学习方式并非运行对抗式辩论，据此提出合作式协议并用组合维度刻画其可学习性，同时分析裁判偶发出错对学习误差的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对计算能力较弱的裁判如何可靠监督高复杂度目标、以及少量判断错误如何放大学习误差的理论刻画，可能为 LVR 中借助不完美验证器训练 latent 推理轨迹与分配贡献提供可供核查的线索，但该文不含视觉或多模态设定，迁移需自行判断。
